sources.title: Diet and body condition of cave-dwelling dwarf crocodiles (Osteolaemus tetraspis, Cope 1861) in Gabon
sources.version: African Journal of Ecology 55(4):411–422 (2017; version of record online 2016-09-28)
sources.locator: Abstract; Abanda cave and surrounding forest comparison.
sources.scope: Local diet and body-condition comparison of cave and forest dwarf crocodiles in Gabon; uses the paper's O. tetraspis name and does not independently resolve later lineage placement.
sources.attribution: Shirley MH, Burtner B, Oslisly R, Sebag D, Testa O (2017). Diet and body condition of cave-dwelling dwarf crocodiles (Osteolaemus tetraspis, Cope 1861) in Gabon. African Journal of Ecology 55(4):411–422. DOI 10.1111/aje.12365. Claims are paraphrased.

sources.title: Species-level diversification of African dwarf crocodiles (Genus Osteolaemus): a geographic and phylogenetic perspective
sources.locator: Abstract; type locality discussion; known-locality sampling and geographic clades.
sources.scope: Multilocus and limited morphological analysis of dwarf crocodiles from known localities; supports three geographic lineages and identifies the O. tetraspis type basin, but does not assign later Abanda cave specimens.
sources.attribution: Eaton MJ, Martin A, Thorbjarnarson J, Amato G (2009). Species-level diversification of African dwarf crocodiles (Genus Osteolaemus): a geographic and phylogenetic perspective. Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution 50(3):496–506. DOI 10.1016/j.ympev.2008.11.009. Claims are paraphrased.

claims.text: The Abanda cave crocodiles studied under the name O. tetraspis ate mainly cave crickets and bats; surrounding forest animals examined ate mainly freshwater crustaceans and insects. Juvenile cave crocodiles had higher body condition than forest juveniles, while the adult comparison was not statistically significant.
claims.scope: Local ecological comparison; small sample size limits adult body-condition inference and does not establish species-wide ecology.

claims.text: Multilocus analyses supported three geographic lineages; the O. tetraspis type specimen originated from the Ogooué River basin in Gabon.
claims.scope: Broad lineage context and type-locality evidence, not a direct genetic assignment of the later Abanda cave samples.

gaps: The relationship between the Abanda cave population and the later three-lineage framework has not been verified using the same specimens.
The cave ecology study does not support a complete species distribution or a range-wide ecological dossier.
